rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct addressees are the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: أي : أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer punishment is worldly affliction: a seven-year famine after the Prophet prayed against them, starvation, smoke-like vision, other calamities, and finally killing or capture at Badr.
rows.anchor: عذاب الدنيا وهو ما محنوا به من القحط سبع سنين بدعاء النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here dun means before the greater punishment, which is punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قبل العذاب الأكبر الذي هو عذاب الآخرة فدون هنا بمعنى قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adna originally describes the lower place of a thing; dun likewise denotes a slightly lower position and is extended to differences in wealth and rank.
rows.anchor: فيقال هذا دون ذلك إذا كان أحط منه قليلا ثم استعير منه للتفاوت

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار والكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashf al-asrar, followed by Kashifi, glosses the greater punishment as the eternal fire, relative to which the worldly punishment is lower.
rows.anchor: وتبعه الكاشفي في تفسيره (فروتر از عذاب بزركتركه خلودست در آتش)

rows.speaker: تفسير نقاش
rows.claim: A report from Naqqash's commentary identifies the lesser punishment as inflation and the greater as the Mahdi's appearance with a sharp sword.
rows.anchor: والرتب درلباب ازتفسير نقاش نقل كرده كه ادنى غلاى اسعارست واكبر خروج مهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations pair worldly humiliation with the Hereafter's misery, or falling into sin with distance from God's nearness.
rows.anchor: وكفته اندخوارى دنيا ونكو نسارىء عقبا يا افتادن دركناه ودور افتادن ازدركاه قرب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian couplet presents separation from union with God as a greater punishment than every burning fire.
rows.anchor: دور ماندن از وصال او عذاب اكبر است آتش سوز فراق ازهر عذابى بدترست

rows.speaker: حقائق البقلي
rows.claim: In Haqa'iq al-Buqli, the lesser punishment is deprivation of gnosis and the greater is veiling from witnessing the Known.
rows.anchor: وفي "حقائق البقلى" : العذاب الأدنى حرمان المعرفة والعذاب الأكبر الاحتجاب عن مشاهدة المعروف

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الوراق
rows.claim: Al-Warraq calls attachment to worldly life the lesser punishment and its resulting chastisement the greater.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن الوراق : الأدنى الحرص على الدنيا والأكبر العذاب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La'all means that those who remain and witness the punishment may return; it can also mean kay, expressing purpose: that they repent of disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: أي : لعل من بقي منهم وشاهده ولعل من مثله بمعنى كي {يرجعون} ويتوبون عن الكفر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: For seekers, a pause from spiritual travel caused by self-admiration, weariness, imagined acceptance, or worldly distraction may bring affliction to awaken them from heedlessness and restore sincere seeking and love.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أرباب الطلب وأصحاب السلوك إذا وقعت لأحدهم في أثناء السلوك وقفة لعجب تداخله أو لملالة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Trials of self, property, home, family, and loved ones can prompt recovery before the greater spiritual punishment of abandonment, estrangement, and a hardened heart.
rows.anchor: ابتلاه الله إما ببلاء في نفسه أو ماله أو بيته من أهاليه وأقربائه وأحبائه لعلهم بإذاقة عذاب البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the shocking improbability of turning away from verses whose clarity and guidance promise happiness in both worlds, like entering a mosque and then not praying there.
rows.anchor: وثم لاستبعاد الإعراض عنها مع غاية وضوحها وإرشادها إلى سعادة الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person described is more unjust than every wrongdoer, although the grammatical form denies the greatest injustice without explicitly denying an equal.
rows.anchor: والمعنى هو أظلم من كل ظالم وإن كان سبك التركيب على نفي الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened class includes everyone characterized by wrongdoing, even when the offense is slight.
rows.anchor: أي : من كل من اتصف بإجرام وإن هانت جريمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sufi reading links return to the verse about hearts being turned, and takes the aim to be renewed sincerity in seeking and height of love.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون إلى صدق طلبهم وعلو محبتهم

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-asrar says naming adopted children after their actual fathers is more just and truthful than calling them by other fathers.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : هو أعدل وأصدق من دعائهم إياهم لغير آبائهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians say that when a conditional sense is impossible, an becomes idh, a particle of past time; thus the past and future forms here do not conflict.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم متى عرض ما يحيل معنى الشرط جعلت أن بمعنى إذ وإذ يكون للماضي

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi explains that lam turns the present verb into a past form and joins it to itself, so the conditional particle governs the combined phrase as if it meant if you left the act.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي في قوله تعالى : {فإن لم تفعلوا} (البقرة : 24) إن تفعلوا جزم بلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their fathers are unknown, those who have accepted Islam are religious brothers and allies; they should be addressed as brother or mawla in religious affection.
rows.anchor: أي : فهم إخوانكم في الدين يعني من أسلم منهم {ومواليكم} وأولياؤكم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hudhayfa had freed and adopted Salim, who had been called Salim ibn Abi Hudhayfa; after this verse, he was called the mawla of Abu Hudhayfa.
rows.anchor: أن أبا حذيفة أعتق عبدا يقال له سالم وتبناه وكانوا يسمونه سالم ابن أبي حذيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janah means sin: as a ship leans toward one side, sin inclines a person away from the truth; the term then came to mean any sin.
rows.anchor: يقال جنحت السفينة أي : مالت إلى أحد جانبيها وسمي الإثم المائل بالإنسان على الحق جناحا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some derive janah from Persian gunah by the Arabic habit of substituting sounds, as with jawhar from gohar.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه معرب كناه على ما هو عادة العرب في الإبدال ومثله الجوهر معرب كوهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza in akhta'tum is a hamzat al-qat' because the if'al verb form has a pronounced hamza.
rows.anchor: بقطع الهمزة لأن همزة باب الأفعال مقطوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pardon covers mistaken naming before the prohibition, slips of the tongue, and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: فيما فعلتموه من ذلك مخطئين قبل النهي أو بعده على سبق اللسان أو النسيان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says naming counts as an error only after the prohibition; khata' is deviation from the proper direction.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : لا تتصف التسمية بالخطأ إلا بعد النهي والخطأ العدول عن الجهة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya distinguishes one who knowingly does wrong as khati from one unaware of the error as mukhti, with usage examples and the verse about none eating except sinners.
rows.anchor: وفرق بين الخاطىء والمخطيء فإن من يأتي بالخطى وهو يعلم أنه خطأ فهو خاطىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is glossed in Persian as concerning that in which you made an error.
rows.anchor: والمعنى بالفارسية : (دران يزى كه خطا كرديد بآن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes ma genitive, coordinated with the earlier ma; another makes it a nominative subject with an omitted predicate, assigning liability to deliberate intent.
rows.anchor: على أن ما محل الجر عطفا على ما أخطأتم أو ما تعمدت قلوبكم فيه الجناح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liability attaches to what the heart deliberately intended after the prohibition.
rows.anchor: أي : ولكن الجناح فيما قصدت قلوبكم بعد النهي

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith warns that anyone who knowingly claims a father other than his own is forbidden Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من دعي إلى غير أبيه وهو يعلم أنه غير أبيه فالجنة عليه حرام"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is abundant in forgiveness and mercy, forgiving error and showing mercy.
rows.anchor: بليغ المغفرة والرحمة يغفر لخطيئتي ويرحم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar heard a man ask God to forgive his sins and answered that one should seek the All-Subduing's forgiveness, since error has already been overlooked.
rows.anchor: وسمع عمر رضي الله عنه رجلا يقول : اللهم اغفر خطاياي فقال : يا ابن آدم استغفر الصمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not contradict the verse: a mistaken person who was negligent and entered into causes leading to the error may still be a fit object of forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: هذا لا يخالف الآية لأن المخطىء إذا قصر ووقع في أسباب أدته إلى الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If an adopter claims as son a person of unknown lineage who is younger than himself, lineage is established; if the person is his slave, he is freed with the established lineage.
rows.anchor: إذا كان مجهول النسب وأصغر سنا من المتبني ثبت نسبه منه وإن كان عبدا له عتق

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: If the adopter is too old to be the claimed child's father, lineage is not established, but Abu Hanifa frees the slave.
rows.anchor: وإن كان لا يولد لمثله لم يثبت النسب ولكنه يعتق عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions disagree: the slave is not freed because an impossible statement is void.
rows.anchor: خلافا لصاحبيه فإنه لا يعتق عندهما لأن كلامه محال فيلغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adoption does not establish new lineage for someone already known to have another lineage, though if he is the adopter's slave he is freed.
rows.anchor: وأما معروف النسب فلا يثبت نسبه بالتبني وإن كان عبدا عتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying the lineage of an adopted child incurs no liability, but denying an established biological child entails li'an for accusing one's wife; retracting the accusation brings a hadd.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن من نفى نسب الدعي عنه لا يلزمه شيء إذ هو ليس بابن له حقيقة

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith says every lineage and noble standing will end except the Prophet's lineage and noble standing.
rows.anchor: كما قال : "كل حسب ونسب ينقطع إلا حسبي ونسبي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring true lineage is connection to the Prophet through poverty and prophethood; one must not sever that bond by abandoning his Sunnah and way.
rows.anchor: فحسبه الفقر ونسبه النبوة فينبغي أن لا يقطع الرحم عن النبوة بترك سنته وسيرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking figurative family ties may be preferable when maintaining them would lead to disbelief or sin.
rows.anchor: إذ ربما يقطع الرحم المجازي إذا كان الوصل مؤديا إلى الكفر أو المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of unveiling divide angels into those who descended from the spirit world into subtle bodies and those who remained disembodied in the spirit world.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الملائكة عند أهل الكشف من أكابر أهل الله على قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first angelic class has subtle bodies, includes the earthly and heavenly angels, and was commanded to prostrate to Adam.
rows.anchor: قسم تنزلوا من مرتبة الأرواح إلى مرتبة الأجسام فلهم أجسام لطيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second class, the absorbed angels, has no bodily covering or awareness of self or other beings because it is wholly immersed in witnessing God; it was not commanded to prostrate.
rows.anchor: وهم المهيمون الذين أشير إليهم بقوله تعالى : {أم كنت من العالين} وهم غير مأمورين بالسجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans surpass both angelic classes in state and perfection because they were created by the hands of Beauty and Majesty, while angels were created by Beauty alone.
rows.anchor: والإنسان أفضل من هذين القسمين في شرف الحال ورتبة الكمال لأنه مخلوق بقبضتي الجمال والجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love entails trial in the world: Adam's descent and worldly hardship are forms of divine education and effects of Majesty.
rows.anchor: العشق يقتضي المحنة وموطنها الدنيا ولذا أهبط آدم من الجنة والمحنة من باب التربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels meant here are initially the embodied first class, who share bodily existence with believers; the honor of the verse also calls for taking the reference generally.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالملائكة ههنا هو القسم الأول لأنهم يشاركون مؤمني البشر في الجمال والوجود الجسماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God and the angels attend to the Prophet's good, display his honor, and magnify his status; God's salat is mercy and the angels' is supplication and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يعتنون بما فيه خيره وصلاح أمره ويهتمون بإظهار شرفه وتعظيم شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusalluna is used by general metaphor, since a homonym cannot simultaneously carry both senses, whether or not those senses conflict.
rows.anchor: فقوله يصلون محمول على عموم المجاز إذ لا يجوز إرادة معنيي المشترك معا

rows.speaker: القهستاني
rows.claim: Al-Qahistani assigns mercy to God's salat, forgiveness to angels, worship and supplication to humans and jinn, and glorification to birds and vermin.
rows.anchor: قال القهستاني : الصلاة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salat is a verbal noun from tasliya, while the ordinary ritual prayer has only the form salat, not a verbal noun tasliya.
rows.anchor: اسم من التصلية وكلاهما مستعمل بخلاف الصلاة بمعنى أداء الأركان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say God's salat is mercy for others but added honor for the Prophet; salat is special while mercy is general, as the verse pairing them shows.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الصلاة من الله تعالى بمعنى الرحمة لغير النبي عليه السلام وبمعنى التشريف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some distinguish the effects: God grants the Prophet praise and support, angels praise and assist him, and believers seek his intercession and follow his Sunnah; for others these are mercy, forgiveness, and supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : صلوات الله على غير النبي رحمة وعلى النبي ثناء ومدحة قولا وتوفيق وتأييد فعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers too should attend to the Prophet with blessings, since they are more deserving of this.
rows.anchor: اعتنوا أنتم أيضا بذلك فإنكم أولى به

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith is cited directing people who bless the Prophet to include others; Bursevi says omitting this leaves the blessing incomplete.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام : "إذا صليتم علي فعمموا" وإلا فقد نقصت الصلاة عليه

rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: Al-Sakhawi says he did not find the cited hadith with that wording; it might mean praying for the Prophet and God's other prophets, whom God sent as He sent him.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام السخاوي في المقاصد الحسنة لم أقف عليه أي : على هذا الحديث بهذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula chooses Allahumma because it is a comprehensive name denoting divinity and suits the Prophet, who gathers the qualities of perfection and mysteries of Beauty and Majesty.
rows.anchor: وخص اللهم ولم يقل يا رب ويا رحمن صل لأنه اسم جامع دال على الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessings raise the Prophet's rank and thereby the community's rank, because a follower's rank depends on the one followed; Rumi expresses this in a cited poem.
rows.anchor: بالصلوات تزيد مرتبة النبي فتزيد مرتبة الأمة لأن مرتبة التابع تابعة لمرتبة المتبوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending blessings also manifests love, since a person mentions what he loves often.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فيها إثبات المحبة ومن أحب شيئا أكثر ذكره

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the present tense to show angels bless continually; imitating them brings a share of their purity and familiarity with the spiritual world.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : صيغة المضارع يعني : {يصلون} (دلالت بر آن ميكندكه ملائكه يوسته دركفتن صلواتند

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
rows.claim: Sahl al-Tustari calls blessings upon Muhammad the best worship because God and the angels perform it before commanding believers to do so.
rows.anchor: قال سهل بن عبد الله التستري قدس سره : الصلاة على محمد أفضل العبادات لأن الله تولاها هو وملائكته

rows.speaker: الصديق الأكبر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr says blessings erase sins more than cold water extinguishes fire and surpass freeing slaves; greeting the Prophet corresponds to God's greeting, better than a thousand good deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الصديق الأكبر رضي الله عنه : الصلاة عليه أمحق للذنوب من الماء البارد للنار وهي أفضل من عتق الرقاب

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti urges reverent blessings without imagining they can discharge any measure of the Prophet's due; they instead seek God's mercy through him.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي صل عليه بالأوقار ولا تجعل له في قلبك مقدار

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith says an angel at the Prophet's grave relays each believer's blessing to him by name and father's name, and God blesses that believer tenfold.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إنملكا أعطاه سمع الخلائق وهو قائم على قبري إذا مت إلى يوم القيامة فليس أحد من أمتي

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: Another hadith says blessings are presented to the Prophet with the sender's name, father's name, tribe, and uncles; proper blessing requires presence of heart and collected attention.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إذا صليتم علي فأحسنوا علي الصلاة فإنكم تعرضون علي بأسمائكم وأسماء آبائكم وعشائركم وأعمامكم"

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual elders say that sending three thousand blessings on Friday night brings a vision of the Prophet in a dream; al-Safi cites this in al-Rashahat.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض الكبار أن من صلى على النبي عليه السلام ليلة الجمعة ثلاثة آلاف رأى في منامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When mounting for a journey, say the basmala and takbir, bless the best of humanity, and recite the travel verses.
rows.anchor: بسم الله والله أكبر وصل على محمد خير البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Mecca road, say takbir while ascending high ground and send blessings when descending.
rows.anchor: بر بلندى رود تكبير بايد كفت وون روى بنشيب آرد صلوات بايد فرستاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Send blessings when touching the Black Stone, at Safa and Marwa, after the talbiya, and while standing at the Sacred Monument.
rows.anchor: وعند استلام الحجر يقول : "اللهم إيمانا بك وتصديقا بكتابك وسنة نبيك" ثم يصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On approaching the Prophet's grave, recite this verse through its end and say صلى الله عليك يا محمد seventy times; an angel replies with the visitor's name and promises the request will not be refused.
rows.anchor: وهفتاد باربكويد صلى الله عليك يا محمد (فرشته ندا كندكه) صلى الله عليك يا فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessings are also prescribed between the grave and pulpit, when the Prophet is mentioned or his name is spoken or written, and by a writer both aloud and in writing.
rows.anchor: ويصلي بين القبر والمنبر ويكبر ويدعو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Begin hadith study and transmission of the Sunnah with a formula of praise, blessing, and peace upon the Prophet, his family, other prophets, and the righteous.
rows.anchor: ويصلي عند ابتداء درس الحديث وتبليغ السنن فيقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Begin admonition and preaching with blessings after praise, since it is a setting for conveying knowledge transmitted from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ويصلي عند ابتداء التذكير والعظة أي : بعد الحمد والثناء لأنه موطن تبليغ العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives a comprehensive blessing formula for Muhammad, his family, wives, and descendants, modeled on God's blessing of Abraham and his family.
rows.anchor: اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك النبي الأمي وعلى آل محمد وأزواجه وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi says the lexicon does not list idha' as the verbal noun of adha, though writers commonly use it.
rows.anchor: يقال : أذى يؤذي أذى وأذية وإذاية ولا يقال إيذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actual suffering is impossible for God; the phrase means doing what God dislikes or rejects, such as disbelief, disobedience, attributing offspring or partners to Him, denying resurrection, or making images in imitation of creation.
rows.anchor: ثم إن حقيقة التأذي وهو بالفارسية : (آزرده شدن) في حقه تعالى محال فالمعنى يفعلون ما يكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal harm to the Messenger includes calling him a poet, sorcerer, soothsayer, or madman, and attacking his marriage to Safiyya.
rows.anchor: بقولهم : شاعر ساحر كاهن مجنون وطعنهم في نكاح صفية الهارونية وهو الأذى القولي

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud recounts that a pagan put camel entrails on the Prophet's shoulders while he prostrated; Fatima removed them, and the Prophet then addressed the Quraysh.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن مسعود (كفت ديدم رسول خدايرا عليه السلام در مسجد حرام درنماز بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical harm included breaking the Prophet's tooth and wounding his face at Uhud, throwing dirt on him, and placing filth on his mantle.
rows.anchor: وكسر رباعيته وشج وجهه الكريم يوم أحد ورمي التراب عليه ووضع القاذورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may refer in reality to harming the Messenger alone, while mentioning God magnifies the Prophet's standing; whoever harms the Messenger harms God, just as obeying him is obeying God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بإيذاء الله ورسوله ايذاء رسول الله خاصة بطريق الحقيقة

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says frequent invocation of al-Kabir helps a debtor repay debt and expand provision; a fasting, deposed person who repeats it a thousand times daily for seven days regains his rank, even if a king.
rows.anchor: قال السهروردي : إذا أكثر منه المديان أدى دينه واتسع رزقه وإن ذكره معزول عن رتبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides from the sky through rain and from the earth through plants; the question is meant to make polytheists admit their idols control not even an atom and God alone provides.
rows.anchor: {يرزقكم من السماوات} بإنزال المطر {والارض} بإخراج النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the polytheists hesitate to answer lest they be compelled by the implication, the Prophet is told to state that God is the provider, the only possible answer.
rows.anchor: وحيث كانوا يتلعثمون في الجواب مخافة الإلزام قيل له عليه السلام : {قل الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision is outward food for bodies or inward knowledge and unveilings for spirits; inward provision is nobler because it yields eternal life, while outward provision gives strength only briefly.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الرزق قسمان : ظاهر وهو الأقوات والأطعمة المتعلقة بالأبدان وباطن وهو المعارف والمكاشفات المتعلقة بالأرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates provision and conveys it to both groups, while distributing it more widely or narrowly as He wills.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى هو المتولي لخلق الرزق والمتفضل بالإيصال إلى كلا الفريقين ولكنه يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith calls seeking lawful livelihood an obligation after the obligations of faith and prayer.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "طلب الحلال فريضة بعد الفريضة" أي : فريضة الإيمان والصلاة

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith says that whoever eats lawful food for forty days will have an illumined heart and springs of wisdom flowing within it.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "من أكل الحلال أربعين يوما نور الله قلبه وأجرى ينابيع الحكمة في قلبه"

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A nightly call from an angel at Jerusalem says that prayers, obligatory or voluntary, are not accepted from one who eats unlawful food.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إنملكا على بيت المقدس ينادي كل ليلة من أكل حراما لم يقبل منه صرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure, lawful food clarifies the heart, increases the light of gnosis, and leads to unveilings and spiritual stations.
rows.anchor: ازباكى مطعم وحلالي قوت صفاى دل خيزد واز صفاى دل نور معرفت افزايد

rows.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
rows.claim: Rumi's verses say lawful food yields light, perfection, knowledge, wisdom, love, tenderness, readiness to serve, and resolve for the next life; unlawful food breeds envy, traps, ignorance, and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: علم وحكمت زايد ازلقمه حلال عشق ورقت آيد از لقمه حلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun iya-kum is coordinated with the noun after inna, yielding the sense that either we or you are on guidance or manifest error.
rows.anchor: {أو إياكم} عطف على اسم أن يعني (باشما)

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَٰلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The competing groups are monotheists worshipping the uniquely providing, inherently powerful God and polytheists worshipping inanimate objects at the lowest level of possibility.
rows.anchor: أي : وأن أحد الفريقين من الذين يوحدون المتوحد بالرزق والقدرة الذاتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding proof, the evenhanded wording silences a stubborn opponent more effectively than directly declaring which side is guided, like a disputant saying one of us is lying.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعد ما سبق من التقرير البليغ الناطق بتعيين من هو على الهدى ومن هو في الضلال أبلغ من التصريح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take aw as waw, yielding: we and you are guided if we believe, or in manifest error if we do not believe.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم أو ههنا بمعنى الواو ، يعني : إنا وإياكم لعلى هدى إن آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prefers aw as deliberate ambiguity displaying fairness, rather than doubt or an attempt to create doubt.
rows.anchor: وأو ههنا لمجرد إبهام وإظهار نصفة لا للشك والتشكيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different prepositions picture the guided person as elevated and able to see, while the astray person is immersed in darkness, a deep pit, or a dungeon without a way out.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الجارين للإيذان بأن الهادي الذي هو صاحب الحق كمن استعلى على مكان مرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurmun, with damma, means sin and originally means cutting; al-Mufradat explains that it was extended to acquiring anything disliked.
rows.anchor: والجرم بالضم الذنب وأصله القطع واستعير لكل اكتساب مكروه كما في "المفردات"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the speakers attribute to themselves is the small lapses and slips no believer avoids; the interlocutors' deeds refer to disbelief and major sins, though each person answers for his own work.
rows.anchor: أي : فعلنا واكتسبنا من الصغائر والزلات التي لا يخلو منها مؤمن {ولا نسأل عما تعملون} من الكفر والكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is more fair and less disputatious because the speakers call even a minor lapse a sin in themselves, while describing the opponents' greater crimes neutrally as deeds.
rows.anchor: وهذا أبلغ في الإنصاف وأبعد من الجدل والاعتساف حيث أسند فيه الإجرام وإن أريد به الزلة وترك الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather both parties on Resurrection for assembly and judgment.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة عند الحشر والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To open between the parties means to judge and decide once each side's state appears, sending the truthful to Paradise and the false to Hell.
rows.anchor: أي : يحكم بيننا ويفصل بعد ظهور حال كل منا ومنكم بأن يدخل المحقين الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fattah is the judge who resolves closed or difficult cases, and al-Alim knows the proper judgment and the parties it concerns.
rows.anchor: {وهو الفتاح} الحاكم الفيصل في القضايا المنغلقة أي : المشكلة {العليم} بما ينبغي أن يقضي به

rows.speaker: الزروقي
rows.claim: Al-Zarruq describes al-Fattah as the gracious one who brings goodness and expansion after constriction, opening doors in worldly and otherworldly affairs for spirits and bodies.
rows.anchor: قال الزروقي الفتاح المتفضل بآإظهار الخير والسعة على أثر ضيق وانغلاق باب للأرواح

rows.speaker: بعض المشايخ
rows.claim: Some shaykhs define al-Fattah as opening constriction: settling disputes, relieving distress through kindness, ignorance through teaching, and poverty through giving.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المشايخ : الفتاح من الفتح وهو الإفراج عن الضيق كالذي يفرج تضايق الخصمين

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali says God's care opens every closed matter and guidance discloses every difficulty; God opens kingdoms for prophets and cites His clear opening for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي رحمه الله : الفتاح هو الذي بعنايته ينفتح كل منغلق وبهدايته ينكشف كل مشكل

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali also describes God removing veils from saints' hearts and opening the heavenly kingdom and the beauty of majesty, citing the verse that none can withhold God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وتارة يرفع الحجاب عن قلوب أوليائه ويفتح لهم الأبواب إلى ملكوت سمائه

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Since God holds the keys of the unseen and provision, He is most fittingly al-Fattah; a servant should seek to help people unlock divine, religious, and worldly difficulties.
rows.anchor: ومن بيده مفاتيح الغيب ومفاتيح الرزق فبالأحرى أن يكون فتاحا وينبغي أن يتعطش العبد
